text:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary deploy failed for service `model-api` (canary=canary-42) - 40% HTTP 503 at t+3m. Metrics: latency spike and 5xx. Logs attached to job 987654.

incident-bot: Paging eng-infra on-call: @josh (oncall) - high-severity canary failure for model-api, possible bad image/tag.

josh (oncall): I'm awake, grabbing it. Can someone paste the deploy job link and the image tag used?

maya: Deploy job here: https://ci.internal/redwood/pipelines/987654/build -> image `gcr.io/redwood/model-api:latest` (pipeline says built from commit `a1b2c3d`). I had flipped the canary to `latest` temporarily for a quick fix earlier. Sorry, was trying to patch the quantization layer.

nora: Canary logs show an immediate mismatch in model weights loader - segfaults on startup in 2 pods. Pulling image locally reproduced a different digest than the release SHA. Looks like `latest` was pointing to an image built on top of an old base layer with incompatible CUDA ABI.

kevin: There's a known CI cache issue where buildpacks can reuse outdated layers if `--cache-from` points to mutable tags. I think the `latest` tag got a layered cache poison.

josh (oncall): OK prioritize rollback. Is there a pinned release tag we can revert the canary to? Also, can we flip the runtime feature flag to disable the new runtime path to reduce customer impact?

maya: Release tag `release-2026-03-15-abcdef1` is the last known-good image. Feature flag is `runtime_new_v2` under LaunchDarkly. I can flip it now if you want.

josh (oncall): Do it. Also start rollback on canary and scale down the bad pods. Commands I'm going to run:```bash
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/model-api --to-revision=24
kubectl -n prod set image deployment/model-api model-api=gcr.io/redwood/model-api:release-2026-03-15-abcdef1
kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/model-api
```

maya: Flipped feature flag `runtime_new_v2` -> off (LD: flag://runtime_new_v2). Confirmed.

deploy-bot: Rollout undo initiated by josh. Job 112233 started.

nora: While rollback happens, I'm pulling artifacts from GCR: `gcloud container images describe gcr.io/redwood/model-api:latest --show-package_vulnerability` shows digest `sha256:deadbeef...`. `release-2026-03-15-abcdef1` has digest `sha256:feedface...`. They are different.

kevin: I'm checking CI: build 987654 log snippet shows `--cache-from gcr.io/redwood/model-api:latest` in docker build, so the freshest layer reused old base. The builder didn't invalidate the layer when the CUDA base changed. Possible cache poisoning.

josh (oncall): Good catch. That explains mismatch. For short-term mitigation: hold canary rollback and scale canary down to 0, then promote the pinned release to canary and re-run health checks. Also notify support and product that some customer calls may have seen 502/503s.

support-bot: Notifying Support: Creating ticket for impacted customers who called model-api between 12:13 and 12:20 UTC. Will update with scope once you confirm.

maya: I've pushed the pinned image to the canary deployment:```bash
kubectl -n prod set image deployment/model-api-canary model-api=gcr.io/redwood/model-api:release-2026-03-15-abcdef1
kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/model-api-canary
```Canary pods starting, health checks showing 200s on /healthz.

deploy-bot: Canary stabilized: success rate 99.8% over 2 minutes.

josh (oncall): OK, scaling original canary back to desired replica counts and promoting release to primary with a controlled rollout. Plan: promote release-2026-03-15-abcdef1 to primary in 10m if no regressions. Also we'll schedule a follow-up to fix CI cache flags.

nora: I'll open a JIRA to change build config: remove `--cache-from latest` and use immutable digests, plus add a post-build `skopeo inspect` verification to assert digest matches expected manifest. Ticket RED-5432.

kevin: For longer term, add a CI step to forbid pushing to `latest` from non-release pipelines and require a signed tag for production images. Also add an automated scan for mutable tags used as cache sources.

support-bot: Support ticket created: #INC-1128. Customers with elevated SLAs: acct-705 and acct-502 might have seen failures. Support will send proactive note referencing incident ID `infra-canary-2123456789`.

maya: Quick postmortem notes: root cause = mutable tag (`latest`) used as cache source during docker build; cache reused incompatible base layer; deployed `latest` to canary; runtime path incompatibility caused startup failures -> 503s. Mitigations executed: feature flag flip, canary rollback, promoted good image, support notified.

josh (oncall): Thanks team. Handoff: I'm going offline in ~30m. @nora take incident owner for follow-up (CI fixes + JIRA) and @kevin for buildsystem changes. We'll run a 30-min blameless postmortem meeting at 16:00 UTC.

nora: Got it, I'll own follow-ups and tracking. Adding notes to the incident doc: https://docs.internal/incidents/infra-canary-2123456789

kevin: I'll schedule a runbook change for CI images. Also creating a small alert that triggers if `latest` ever appears in production image tags.

josh (oncall): Final status: services healthy, canary and primary stable, customer impact limited to a small window. Closing paging. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Incident `infra-canary-2123456789` resolved by josh at 12:42 UTC.

nora: Adding retrospective notes and RCA to the incident doc now.

support-bot: Support notified customers and updated ticket #INC-1128 with mitigation steps.

maya: Sorry for the churn. Will avoid using `latest` in prod pipelines. :bow:
